description:
n + 1 with both operands known integers lowers to a direct call of Kernel.+ whose result is delivered to a resume entry: the caller is split in two, the rest of the body's live values are captured in a closure, and fz_op_add_ii runs behind deliver_lanes. Seen in the backend dump of walk(<<c, r :: binary>>, n) -> walk(r, n + 1): 'tail direct_call +(v1, 1) -> deliver e1', e1 captures r. About 26% of the plain walk after inline reads.

Investigated (read-only, develop at 76cf77155):
- First departure from 'one add': the front end. A binary operator in a body is a call to a Kernel function (src/compiler2/jobs/body.rs, Expr::BinOp via direct_operator_name: + - * / % == != < <= > >=), before any type is known. fz_ir has no add/sub/mul primitive.
- Every non-tail call splits. plan_steps/plan_continuation (jobs/body.rs) make a DeliveredResume entry unless the call is the last thing in its block. There is no leaf or plain-return call form; no property of the callee is consulted. EffectSummary has no consumer but the dump.
- After planning, Kernel.+[int,int] is one tail call to the extern wrapper of fz_op_add_ii (checked return: i64 overflow raises ArithmeticError; there are no bignums). So the chain is caller -> +[int,int] -> wrapper -> runtime fn -> return_call_indirect into the continuation closure.
- Same position: - * / % div rem, < <= > >= ==, byte_size, length, elem, hd, tl, tuple_size, abs, <> (guarded Kernel functions over an extern). and/or/not are inlined as case. The same operators in a guard are inline PatternGuardExpr nodes with no call.
- In four backend dumps, about 100 of 213 delivered call sites are Kernel operators and scalar wrappers.
- Existing parts that could serve: native lowering already turns an entry with a single direct transfer into a block of the transferring function (EntryFns::for_entries); guards already emit an extern inline (lower_guard_extern); the checked-extern wrapper is already 'one primitive, raise on failure'. Candidate rule: in native lowering, a delivered call whose target resolves to an extern wrapper is the extern call, its failure check, and a direct transfer to the resume entry, which then becomes a block. The interpreter is unchanged.
- A test can pin a call site's return flow through BackendProgramCapture (src/compiler2/drive_test.rs).

Size in the distiller (profile, 16,000 lines): closure capture and code reads are about 3.5% of samples in runtime calls; the share inside compiled code is not measured. Map puts (23%) and field reads (10%) come first. Next step: a spike of the candidate rule on the walk and the distiller with a prediction, then a proposal page. Evidence: scratchpad b183-5/walkd.backend, walkd.clif; arith/tally.py.
title: Arithmetic on known integers does not go through a continuation
